title: AI Isn't Replacing Developers - Here's Why
summary: Veteran developer compares AI to the early web: overhyped but a big opportunity; learn fundamentals plus the AI stack.

assertions.quote: Jevons paradox will kick in ... a lot more software is going to be created

verdicts.note: Jevons effects are historically common and plausible for software, but whether demand growth outpaces productivity for developer headcount is unproven.

assertions.quote: big companies have fired everybody and then they found out the AI is woof

verdicts.note: There are reports of AI-motivated cuts being reversed (e.g. Klarna support staff) and analyst forecasts of rehiring, but broad 'boomerang' rehiring of engineers is weakly evidenced.

assertions.quote: It's a power tool for competent users

verdicts.note: Experts get more reliable results and catch errors, but several RCTs show larger measured speedups for juniors, and METR found experts slowed; contested.

assertions.quote: this is not the end of software development, it is the beginning of a brand new boom

verdicts.note: Through 2026 evidence points to role change and slower junior hiring, not elimination of the profession; long-run is uncertain.

assertions.quote: Design patterns are hugely important in the AI age of software development

verdicts.note: DORA 2025 found AI amplifies existing engineering practices; strong fundamentals predict AI benefit.
